kp.k: Law-firm-owned ALSP offers AI software alongside expert services
kp.d: On April 15, 2026, ClearyX, an alternative legal and business services provider owned by Cleary Gottlieb, announced CX+, comprising CX+Insights and CX+Transact for in-house teams and deal professionals. The announcement describes a delivery model allowing standalone software licensing or software paired with ClearyX services, with flexible pricing but no specified prices.
qs: ClearyX, an alternative legal and business services provider owned by global law firm Cleary Gottlieb, today announced the launch of [CX+](https://clearyx.legal/cx/), a proprietary, AI-powered contract insights and due diligence platform.
CX+ can be licensed as a standalone tool with accessible, flexible pricing models or paired with wrap-around services from ClearyX’s expert team.

kp.k: Client co-development targets specific legal workflow problems
kp.d: ClearyX says senior in-house clients and legal operations professionals co-developed CX+, with features based on documented pain points and validated against daily use cases. CEO Carla Swansburg attributes the product to years of client conversations and argues that generic tools do not solve the targeted problems.
qs: CX+ was co-developed with senior in-house clients and legal operations professionals, with each feature designed around documented pain points and validated against the use cases legal teams encounter daily.
“We spent years speaking with clients about the problems that they wish technology would solve for them, and that generic tools simply aren’t solving,”

kp.k: Contract intelligence becomes an embedded, continuously updated layer
kp.d: CX+Insights is presented as enabling in-house teams to query contract portfolios using AI question bundles and generate dashboards, playbooks, risk analyses and visualizations. ClearyX describes direct repository connections without contract migration and automatic analytics updates as documents are added, positioning the product as an ongoing intelligence layer within existing legal technology rather than a separate system.
qs: The platform allows legal teams to load contracts, query documents using AI question bundles, and surface actionable insights through custom dashboards, playbooks, risk analyses, and visualizations.

CX+Insights connects directly to existing document repositories, without requiring contract migration, and, as documents are added, automatically feeds results live into its built-in analytics platform.

Its open architecture is designed not as a standalone solution, but as a permanent intelligence layer within a legal team’s existing technology stack, sitting between raw contract data and the business decisions that depend on it.

kp.k: AI diligence combines review tooling and service-provider collaboration
kp.d: ClearyX describes CX+Transact as supporting contract review and M&A due diligence through tabular review, tagging, filtering, editing, customizable prompts and diligence workflows. Its portals provide review-progress visibility, centralized data and direct collaboration with ClearyX, connecting software-supported work with the provider’s service delivery.
qs: CX+Transact is purpose-built for contract review and M&A due diligence.

It’s core features include a tabular review system with tagging, filtering, and in-place editing, diligence-focused workflows, customizable AI prompt templates, and CX Diligence Portals that give users real-time visibility into review progress, centralized data access, and direct collaboration with ClearyX.

kp.k: ClearyX reports 40-60% diligence savings across 150+ deals
kp.d: The company announcement reports documented cost and time savings of 40-60% on due diligence compared to manual review across 150+ deals. This is a ClearyX-reported operational result; the document does not specify the observation period, measurement methodology or independent validation.
qs: Across 150+ deals, ClearyX has documented consistent cost and time savings of 40-60% on due diligence compared to manual review.

kp.k: Adaptability and integration underpin the proposed deployment model
kp.d: ClearyX describes CX+ as model-agnostic and configurable to client requirements and workflows. It claims secure code, testing for accuracy and stability, and native integrations through custom APIs enable deployment within existing systems; these are product-design claims rather than reported test results.
qs: CX+ is model-agnostic and highly adaptable, giving clients the flexibility to configure it around their own requirements and workflows.
Security is foundational, and the software is designed from the ground up with secure code and rigorous testing for accuracy and stability.
Native integrations with existing document management systems and source repositories via custom APIs mean clients can start realizing value from day one.

kp.k: Leadership frames AI as augmenting human expertise
kp.d: Michael Gerstenzang, Cleary Gottlieb Senior Partner and a founder of ClearyX, argues that excellent client service increasingly requires embedding AI into legal work. He frames CX+ as augmenting human expertise to improve insights and outcomes, rather than asserting autonomous replacement of lawyers.
qs: Increasingly, delivering excellence to clients requires embedding AI into your work.
CX+ is built to augment human expertise to drive clearer insights and efficient, impactful outcomes.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: ClearyX reports 40–60% cost and time savings on transactional due diligence compared with manual review.
pts.d: In the CX+Transact section of its company announcement, ClearyX attributes consistent due diligence savings to its experience across more than 150 deals. CX+Transact is presented as an AI-powered contract review and M&A due diligence product with structured review, customizable prompts, progress visibility, and collaboration with ClearyX. The announcement does not specify whether all reported deals used the newly launched product.

pts.k: ClearyX claims AI can turn existing contract portfolios into continuously updated intelligence for legal and business decisions.
pts.d: The company presents CX+Insights as allowing in-house teams to query contracts through AI question bundles and generate dashboards, playbooks, risk analyses, and visualizations. Its claimed change to legal operations is an ongoing intelligence layer within existing systems rather than a separate repository requiring contract migration.

pts.k: ClearyX claims configurable, integrated AI addresses workflow problems generic tools do not solve and can deliver value immediately.
pts.d: CEO Carla Swansburg attributes the product's workflow fit to years of client conversations and says technology should be applied when it improves work. The company claims model flexibility, customization, and connections to existing repositories permit value from the first day. It offers the platform either as licensed software or combined with expert services, positioning ClearyX as an alternative legal and business services provider offering both technology and service delivery.

pts.k: Michael Gerstenzang claims excellent client service increasingly requires embedded AI, framed as augmenting human expertise.
pts.d: Gerstenzang, Senior Partner of Cleary Gottlieb and a founder of ClearyX, presents AI adoption as increasingly necessary for client-service excellence. His stated mechanism is augmentation producing clearer insights and more efficient outcomes, not replacement of lawyers or autonomous reliance on AI output.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers internal deal experience, client co-development, and executive statements; it supplies no detailed evaluation methodology.
pts.d: The numerical savings claim rests on ClearyX's reported documentation across 150+ deals, with manual review as the comparator. The announcement does not provide measurement dates, calculation methods, deal characteristics, or independent validation. Workflow-fit claims rest on documented client pain points, use-case validation, and Swansburg's account of years of conversations. Security, accuracy, and stability are supported by assertions about design and testing rather than reported test results. The broader claim about AI's increasing necessity is Gerstenzang's executive judgment.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The claims concern capabilities at the April 15, 2026 launch, prior deal experience, and continuing workflow integration, without a dated forecast.
pts.d: The announcement presents product capabilities as available at launch. The savings figure describes accumulated deal experience but has no stated observation period. Immediate value is linked to native integrations via custom APIs; continuing analytics updates occur as documents are added. Workflow benefits are presented in the context of configuration around client requirements. Gerstenzang's 'increasingly' signals an ongoing trend without a deadline or quantified adoption prediction.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The affected users are corporate legal teams, legal operations professionals, and deal teams, with ClearyX supplying technology and optional expert delivery.
pts.d: In-house lawyers are offered systematic contract intelligence within their existing technology stacks. Deal professionals are offered more efficient contract review and M&A diligence, progress visibility, and direct collaboration with ClearyX. Legal operations professionals participate in product development and are part of the operational audience. ClearyX, a law-firm-owned alternative legal and business services provider, offers software alongside services from its multidisciplinary team. The announcement does not make workforce-reduction, profession-wide employment, or access-to-justice claims.
